Priorities & Progress

My eight priorities for District 6, and a progress report on each one at the start of every quarter.

During my campaign, I called my early-reading goal “The Third Grade Standard.”

Progress, four times a year

A progress report on every priority at the start of each quarter, in January, April, July and October, so residents can follow the work all year long.

  1. Q1JanuaryFirst report
  2. Q2AprilSecond report
  3. Q3JulyThird report
  4. Q4OctoberFourth report

The eight priorities

  1. Early Literacy and Third-Grade Reading

    Reading by the end of third grade decides how school goes from then on. I'll keep third-grade reading in front of the Board, ask for the numbers school by school, and report what I learn back to District 6 every quarter. I'm one of nine commissioners, so I'll say plainly what I can move and what depends on the district.

    Early Literacy

  2. Early Literacy Instruction and Structured Literacy

    How reading is taught in kindergarten through third grade matters as much as how often. I'll ask in public session which approach the district uses and what results it's getting, and I'll keep pressing for structured literacy practices in every early classroom. Curriculum belongs to the district, so my job is to ask the questions and keep the answers public.

    Early Literacy

  3. Early Intervention

    A child who falls behind should be noticed early, not after retention is the only option left. I'll ask how quickly students are identified and what support follows, and I'll push for that data to be reported to the Board and made public. Support happens at the school level, so I'll keep the answers visible and follow up.

    Student Achievement

  4. School Improvement Goals

    A goal only means something if the public can see it and check it. I'll ask that schools in District 6 publish clear, measurable improvement goals each year and share regular progress updates in public session. The goals are set by district and school leaders, and the Board's role is oversight.

    Student Achievement

  5. Safe and Supportive Learning Environments

    Students learn when they feel secure, and teachers teach better when expectations are clear. I'll ask for school climate and discipline data to be reported to the Board and published, and I'll raise conditions I see in District 6 schools on the public record. I don't run individual schools or handle student matters, but I can make sure the Board is looking at the right information.

    Safe & Supportive Schools

  6. Annual Literacy Growth Reports

    A commitment nobody reports on can't be checked by anyone. I'll ask the district for annual literacy reporting, and I'll publish here what I have and say plainly what I don't. You'll always know where a number came from.

    Accountability & Stewardship

  7. Quarterly Town Halls

    Residents should have a predictable place to raise something and get answered in public. I'll hold a town hall in District 6 every quarter and publish a summary afterward, including what was asked and what follow-up is owed. What the district does with what's raised is out of my hands, so I'll keep following up until residents get an answer.

    Family & Community Engagement

  8. Public Performance Dashboard

    Information the public can't find can't hold anyone accountable. I'll keep the numbers on this site current, with every figure tied to a named district or state source. I'll also ask the district to improve its own public reporting, since a district-wide dashboard is theirs to build.

    Accountability & Stewardship

How each report works

Timing
Reports are published at the start of every quarter: January, April, July and October.
Sources
A figure appears only when it comes from a published source, and that source is named.
Evidence
Where a document, dataset or official record supports an entry, the entry links to it and shows the date it was last checked.
Control
Each priority separates what I directly control from what I can influence and what depends on the district. I am one vote of nine on a board that acts together.

Sources: MSCS Board of Education; my campaign platform, voteharris901.com (campaign wording only).
